module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.Defs

@[expose] public section

open Matrix
open scoped MatrixGroups

variable (n : Type*) [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

/-- The multiplicative group homomorphism `(Rˣ)ⁿ →* GL(n, R)` given by mapping a vector `x` to
`Matrix.diagonal x`. -/
def Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.diagonalHom : (n → Rˣ) →* GeneralLinearGroup n R where
  toFun := fun d ↦ ⟨Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ d i), Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ (d i).inv), by simp, by simp⟩
  map_mul' x y := by ext; simp [-mul_diagonal, -diagonal_mul]
  map_one' := by ext; simp

/-- The group of invertible diagonal matrices. -/
def Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.diagonalSubgroup : Subgroup (GeneralLinearGroup n R) :=
  Subgroup.map (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.diagonalHom n R) ⊤

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2504.17644/Margulis.lean:89–96, the quotient uses the range of SpecialLinearGroup.map (polyToLaurent F). However, polyToLaurent embeds the polynomial variable as X in Mathlib's X-adically topologized F⸨X⸩. The source's polynomial variable t must instead map to X⁻¹, giving the subring F[X⁻¹], not F[X]. This is not a harmless variable renaming: /workspace/review/use_site.lean proves that I + X⁻¹ E₀₁ belongs to the corrected SL₄ subgroup but not the implemented one, and that the implemented images of polynomial-variable powers converge to zero. Indeed, the current subgroup H lies inside the compact open subgroup C = SL₄(F[[X]]). Every diagonal orbit projects to an infinite subset of the discrete space G/C: its stabilizer in the closed noncompact diagonal group is compact and therefore has infinite index. Consequently no such orbit in G/H has compact closure, contrary to the asserted existence. The reviewed diagonal subgroup definitions themselves are correct; this is a separate downstream embedding error.
findings.source_evidence: Huang–Shi, Bounded diagonal orbits in homogeneous spaces over function fields, arXiv:2504.17644v3, §1 immediately before Theorem 1.2 (https://arxiv.org/e-print/2504.17644v3; bounded_orbits.tex:229–241), specifies K = F((t⁻¹)) with |b tˡ| = pˡ, then asserts a nonclosed relatively compact diagonal orbit in SL₄(K)/SL₄(F[t]) for characteristics 3, 5, 7, 11. Mathlib/RingTheory/LaurentSeries.lean defines the X-adic valued structure and proves valuation_single_zpow: v(single m 1) = exp(-m), so its positive-degree Laurent variable corresponds to the source's t⁻¹.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Margulis.polyToLaurent with the polynomial homomorphism sending the variable to the inverse Laurent parameter: `Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (algebraMap F F⸨X⸩) (HahnSeries.single (-1 : ℤ) (1 : F))`. Keep the usual Laurent-series topology and use this corrected map in the lattice subgroup. This expression and the distinguishing subgroup witness compile in /workspace/review/use_site.lean.

reformulations.difference: Defines the subgroup as the image of vectors of ring units under diagonalHom, rather than directly requiring that an invertible matrix have zero off-diagonal entries. Over a general commutative ring, the unit-entry parameterization might appear to impose an extra restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every declared finite index type and commutative ring, proved `g ∈ diagonalSubgroup n R ↔ (g : Matrix n n R).IsDiag`. The forward direction follows because diagonalHom produces a diagonal matrix. Conversely, a diagonal g equals diagonal (diag g); since g is a matrix unit, Mathlib's isUnit_diagonal makes diag g a unit in the product ring. MulEquiv.piUnits then supplies the vector of component units whose diagonalHom image is g. The proof covers empty indices, singleton indices, rings with zero divisors, and the zero ring without additional hypotheses.

review.notes: Both declarations in the reviewed library module are faithful, and no duplicate Mathlib declaration was found. Its determinant-one comap also has the expected diagonal meaning.
